scenario: A mountain-rescue programme selects trainees if they have either elite climbing skill or elite wilderness first-aid skill. A 5% diversity wildcard also selects trainees with neither trait. Trainers infer a negative relationship between climbing and first-aid skill among the selected class.

data.description: Selection is based on either strength plus a wildcard.

question: Among selected trainees, compute (a) P(climbing | first-aid, selected), and (b) P(climbing | not first-aid, selected). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The selected class shows collider bias even though the population traits are independent.

naive_answer: Selected trainees who are strong in first aid seem less likely to be strong climbers, so the skills probably trade off.
naive_trap: Selection on either capability creates a spurious negative association.
